**B. Two rigs, one damage slot.** Before: damage a Black Clinic 12, switch to a Field Kit and damage it 5, switch back, and the Black Clinic reads 40/40 with `hpSpent` overwritten to 5 under `hpTier:"Field Kit"`. After, using the case the tier key could never express at all (two Black Clinics): damage #1 by 12 and #2 by 31 through the real buttons and both hold, `hp = {eq_x0lisa8:12, eq_tx09gyp:31}`. Switching between them, detouring through the Scrap Rig and back, and repairing one all leave the other untouched. A REPAIR to zero and the FULL button delete the entry rather than leaving a 0.

Also reproduced before the fix, in `app/js/inventory.js`: two Black Clinics with one live printed the Fabrication bench chip **twice**, "Advanced Medkit (Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]) · BASIC". And the picker: recorded `Combat Grade`, owning only a Field Kit, the engine resolved Field Kit while the `<select>` sat on index 0 showing "- No Rig -". Both now correct: one chip; picker shows the resolved Field Kit.

## Resolvers that now exist

Exactly one: `rigStats(ch)` in `app/js/engine.js` (~line 1318). It answers with an equipment **entry key**, so the answer names one specific object.

- `ownedRigTiers` became `ownedRigs(ch)`, returning `{key, row}` pairs with the same-tier dedupe removed. Ownership is decided in this one function.
- `ownedRigTier(ch)` (the dead singular resolver) is **deleted**.
- The picker consumes `d.rig.rigKey` and `d.rig.ownedRigs`; option values are `"key:<entryKey>"`. `traumaRigKids` now takes only the derived record, with no `ch` in scope, so it cannot grow a second reading of storage again.
- `tbKits` compares each row's own `entryKey(e)` against the resolved `rigKey` and has **no ownership predicate of its own for rigs** (the `qty > 0` check now applies only to real kit rows), so nothing is left to drift from the engine.
- Both integrity controls (`app/js/combat.js`, `app/js/grid.js`) write under `t.rigKey`. Swapping rigs no longer zeroes damage, which was the write that used to mask the shared slot.

## Migration (`app/js/store.js`, beside the other `ch.rig` defaults)

`{tier, scrap, hpSpent, hpTier}` -> `{key, scrap, hp}`. Twelve shapes were run through `importCharacter`, which calls the same `migrate`:

- owned `tier` -> that entry's `key`; **unowned `tier` -> dropped** (the engine was already ignoring it, and it cannot return because a re-bought rig is a new entry)
- `hpSpent > 0` with an owned `hpTier` -> `hp[thatEntryKey]`; unowned or absent `hpTier` -> **dropped**, per the ruling that an unattributable rig arrives full
- `hp` entries whose key has left the equipment list are **pruned on every load**, and a `key` whose entry is gone is cleared, so neither can accumulate across a campaign
- no `ch.rig`, `hp` already present, `rig` as an array or a string, `key`/`tier` as numbers, `hpSpent` as a string, `hpTier` as an object, `hp` values that are strings/negative/NaN: all normalize without throwing. An over-track stored value stays stored and the engine clamps it (999 on a Field Kit reads 0/15).

Seeded `hp:{eqA:12, eqGONE:40, eqDEAD1:5, eqDEAD2:7}` with `key:"eqGONE"`; after a forced reload: `hp:{eqA:12}`, `key:null`. `engine.js` loads before `store.js` (app/index.html:77-78) and `load()` is called from `app.js:125`, so the `EN.engine && EN.engine.ownedRigs` guard at `store.js:269` never degrades to `[]` and never wipes live damage.

## FINDING 1 (collision, confirmed) — a rig entry with no `id` keys on its NAME, so two of them share one key, one damage slot, and one picker option

`app/js/engine.js:871` — `entryKey(e) { return (e && (e.id || e.name)) || null; }`. The whole refactor rests on this returning an instance id. It falls back to the catalog name, and `app/js/store.js:364` refuses to assign an id to an entry whose `qty` is not `> 0`:

    if (e.id || !(e.qty > 0) || isStackableName(e.name)) { splitEquipment.push(e); return; }

while `app/js/engine.js:1315` admits that same entry as owned:

    if (!e || (e.qty != null && e.qty <= 0)) return;

The two predicates disagree about a **missing** `qty`: the split says "not > 0, skip", the engine says "not != null, keep". So `{name: "Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"}` is a permanently name-keyed live rig, on every load, forever.

Failing scenario, run live at `http://localhost:8793/app/` with class Stitcher, `equipment: [{name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"},{name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"}]`, `rig: {}` (via the real `store.importCharacter`, then the real Freelancer controls):

- `ownedRigs` returns two rows with the identical key `"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"`.
- The real picker renders two options with the **same value**, both matching the resolved key, and the browser lands on the last one:

      key:Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5] || Black Clinic [5] #1 ... || sel=false
      key:Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5] || Black Clinic [5] #2 ... || sel=true   <- selectedIndex 3

  The engine resolved row #1; the picker says #2. Selecting #1 writes the same string and the picker snaps straight back to #2. Rig #1 is unaddressable.
- Real `- DAMAGE` with amount 12: `hp = {"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]": 12}`, and **both** rows read `28/40`. This is verbatim the "one damage slot for all rigs" bug that DEFERRED-FIXES.md:237 marks fixed.
- The Fabrication bench prints the chip **twice**, verbatim the repro DEFERRED-FIXES.md:220-223 marks fixed:

      Advanced Medkit (Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]) · BASIC
      Advanced Medkit (Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]) · BASIC

  `tbKits` (`app/js/inventory.js:1789`) admits a row iff `entryKey(e) === liveRigKey`, and both rows satisfy it, so removing the bench's own predicate did not help here.
- Drop one of the two and the survivor keeps the dropped rig's damage, because the key is the same string; the prune keeps it because the name is still live.

Fix shape: make ownership and id-assignment agree on a missing `qty` (normalize `e.qty` to 1 in `migrate`, or have the split key off `isStackableName` alone), and/or have `ownedRigs` require a real `e.id` for rigs.

The rig migration calls `EN.engine.ownedRigs(ch)` at `store.js:269`. The legacy split that assigns instance ids runs ~90 lines later at `store.js:361-397`, and it re-keys `equippedWeapons`, `equippedArmor/Shield/Focus`, `carry`, and `slotInert` (lines 381-396) but **not** `ch.rig.key` and **not** `ch.rig.hp`.

## FINDING 1 (high) — `app/js/store.js:269` — the migration runs before entry ids exist, so it keys the pick and the damage on the item NAME

`migrate()` does the `ch.rig` conversion at lines 259-286, calling `EN.engine.ownedRigs(ch)` at line 269. The non-stackable **equipment id split runs 100 lines later, at lines 361-379**, inside the same function. So at line 269 a legacy id-less rig row still has no `id`, and `entryKey(e)` (`app/js/engine.js:871`, `return (e && (e.id || e.name)) || null`) falls back to `e.name`. The migration writes a name into `rg.key` and into `rg.hp`, then the split replaces that row's identity with a fresh `eq_` id. The split's own `nameToIds` remap at lines 381-396 covers `equippedWeapons`, `equippedArmor/Shield/Focus`, `carry` and `slotInert` — **`ch.rig` is the one entry-keyed field it does not remap.**

Failing scenario, run through `EN.store.importCharacter` (which calls the same `migrate`). Legacy Stitcher who deliberately ran the lesser rig and had damaged it:

```
equipment: [{name:"Field Kit Trauma Rig [0]", qty:1}, {name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty:1}]
rig:       {tier:"Field Kit", scrap:false, hpSpent:10, hpTier:"Field Kit"}
```

| | no ids (legacy) | same record WITH ids |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rig` after migrate | `{key:"Field Kit Trauma Rig [0]", hp:{"Field Kit Trauma Rig [0]":10}}` | `{key:"eq_d2", hp:{eq_d2:10}}` |
| rows after migrate | `eq_afti4qy` / `eq_dbwoe60` | `eq_d2` / `eq_d1` |
| resolved | `eq_dbwoe60` **Black Clinic 40/40, Output +3** | `eq_d2` Field Kit 5/15, Output +0 |
| `fromOwnedGear` | true (pick lost, AUTO) | false (pick honoured) |
| **Triage Save DC** | **11** | **8** |

Both guarantees the migration doc claims are violated for exactly the records the migration exists for: the recorded pick is dropped although the tier *is* owned, and 10 points of attributable damage are discarded although `hpTier` *does* name an owned tier. It is not a display-only slip — a derived value moves (DC 8 to 11, Output Bonus +0 to +3). Secondarily, the prune at lines 281-286 uses the pre-split `liveKeys`, so the now-dead name keys survive that pass: `rig.hp` and `rig.key` carry junk for the whole session and clear only on the *next* load, so "pruned on every load" is off by one load for these records.

Fix: move the `ch.rig` block to after line 379, or add `ch.rig.key` / `ch.rig.hp` to the `nameToIds` remap at 381-396.

## FINDING 2 (medium) — entry keys can collide, which re-opens both bugs the refactor closed

`app/js/store.js:364` skips id assignment for any row where `!(e.qty > 0)`. A rig row with no `qty` field therefore **never** gets an id, on this load or any future one, and its `entryKey` stays the item name. Two such rows are indistinguishable.

Failing scenario, driven on the live character: `equipment: [{name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"}, {name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"}]`

(`app/js/inventory.js:1789` matches each row's own key against the resolved key, so both rows match.)
- One shared damage slot: with `hp:{"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]":12}` both read 28/40, so damaging one damages the other — the "two rigs, one damage slot" bug, back.
- The picker renders two `<option>`s with identical `value`, so the two rigs cannot be told apart or picked separately.

Fix: backfill ids for non-stackable rows regardless of `qty`, or give `ownedRigs` a positional tiebreak for id-less rows.

### 1. The migration resolves entry keys BEFORE entry ids exist. `app/js/store.js:269`

The `ch.rig` block runs at lines 259 to 286. The equipment instance-split that mints `eq_` ids runs at **line 361**, a hundred lines later. `entryKey(e)` (`app/js/engine.js:871`) is `e.id || e.name`, so for any record whose rig entry has no `id` yet, `ownedRigs` at line 269 answers with the item NAME, and migrate writes a `key` and `hp` keys that the split then invalidates.

Traced live, with a setter on `rig.key` to prove only `migrate` wrote it:

```
"Field Kit Trauma Rig [0]" <- at migrate (store.js:276:36) at importCharacter (store.js:502:5)
```

| imported (equipment entries carry no `id`) | stored after migrate | equipment after split | engine reads |
|---|---|---|---|
| `{tier:"Black Clinic", hpSpent:12, hpTier:"Black Clinic"}` | `key:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"`, `hp:{"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]":12}` | `eq_ficpdso` | **40/40, AUTO** |
| owns FK + BC, `{tier:"Field Kit", hpSpent:10, hpTier:"Field Kit"}` | same, name-keyed | `eq_s1k8wb8`, `eq_49gknr1` | **Black Clinic** 40/40, Output **+3** instead of the picked Field Kit's +0 |

Both spec clauses fail on exactly the legacy shape the migration exists to convert: damage whose `hpTier` names an owned tier is **not** attributed, and an owned `tier` does **not** become that entry's key. It also is **not idempotent**: load 1 stores name keys, load 2 prunes them (`store.js:281-286`), so the damage is destroyed rather than merely misfiled. Confirmed by three successive loads: `P2 → key:null, hp:{}`.

Reachability, stated honestly: no roster this app wrote can hold both shapes, because the split shipped in `bd28d01` (2026-07-03) and rigs in `bf44843` (2026-08-09), and every in-app insert path sets an id (`inventory.js:106`, `builder.js:993`). The live vector is a hand-edited or third-party JSON through `importCharacter`, plus finding 3 below, which is the same root cause and does not need a legacy record at all. Fix: move the `ch.rig` block after line 397, or re-key `rig.key`/`rig.hp` inside the split's own re-key pass at `store.js:380-396`, which already re-keys `equippedWeapons`, `equippedArmor/Shield/Focus`, `carry`, and `slotInert` from name to id and simply omits `ch.rig`.

### 2. The new equipment read throws, and `load()` answers by discarding the whole roster. `app/js/store.js:269` -> `app/js/engine.js:1314`

`((ch && ch.equipment) || []).forEach` has no `Array.isArray` guard, unlike migrate's own equipment handling at line 361.

```
importCharacter with ch.equipment = { "0": {id:"eq_x", name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", qty:1} }
  -> TypeError: ((ch && ch.equipment) || []).forEach is not a function
```

Through `load()` the blast radius is total. With 32 records in `localStorage`, corrupting **one** record's `equipment` into an object: the `catch` at `store.js:446-449` runs `state.roster = {}`, measured `recordsBefore:32, recordsAfterLoad:0, activeId:null`, and the next `persist` writes `{}` over the file. Before this refactor migrate never touched `ch.equipment` this early, so this is a new instance. In fairness it is not a new class: `(ch.cyberware || []).forEach` at `store.js:289` wipes the roster the same way, verified (`recordsAfterLoad:0`). The rig block is now merely the earliest unguarded read.

### 3. Two rigs can still share one damage slot, no legacy record required. `app/js/engine.js:1315`

The split at `store.js:364` skips any entry failing `e.qty > 0`, so an entry with **no `qty` field** never gets an id. `ownedRigs` accepts it anyway: `if (!e || (e.qty != null && e.qty <= 0)) return;` passes on `undefined`. Both then key on the name, permanently, and the name IS in `liveKeys`, so migration never cleans it up.

```
equipment: [{name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"}, {name:"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"}]
ownedKeys: ["Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]", "Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]"]
damage one by 17  ->  hp: {"Black Clinic Trauma Rig [5]": 17}  ->  BOTH read 23/40
```

That is the exact defect the refactor was written to close (one damage slot for two rigs), plus two picker options at `combat.js:1314` carrying an identical `value`, so the player cannot address the second rig. Same root cause as finding 1: the `e.id || e.name` fallback is being trusted as an instance identity by both the engine and the migration. Either make `ownedRigs` require a real `id`, or have the split normalize a missing `qty` to 1.

### 4. Nit: `rig.key === ""` is never normalized. `app/js/store.js:266`, `276`, `286`

`typeof "" === "string"` survives line 266, `!rg.key` skips line 276, and `rg.key &&` skips the line 286 clear, so an empty-string key persists through every future load. Harmless today: `rigStats` treats it as no pick and falls to AUTO. I saw one in-session record reach `key:""` and could not reproduce the write, so I am not claiming a writer; the only expression in the app that yields it is `v.slice(4)` at `combat.js:1329` on an empty `select` value. Worth a one-token guard, not worth a hunt.
